name: Death-state partition
summary: Death remains legible when transient run state, recoverable state, durable profile state, world mutation, and player knowledge have separately declared reset rules.
player_action: The player dies, inspects the consequence, and begins another attempt.
system_response: The game applies a visible state partition instead of treating every owned, learned, unlocked, and world-level value as one save blob.
failure_modes: The player cannot predict which category an item belongs to.
A crash applies only part of the death transition.
The interface reports retained state that the simulation removed.
accessibility: Describe retained and lost categories without relying on color alone.
Provide confirmation and recovery paths for destructive profile actions.

smallest_playable_test.setup: A ten-minute run containing one transient resource, one recoverable resource, one durable unlock, one world mutation, one learned journal entry, forced death, save/reload, and crash injection.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Every transition matches the declared partition and players can explain the next attempt without external documentation.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: State is technically consistent but consequence remains surprising or administratively heavy.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Any seed produces partial loss, duplication, or disagreement between simulation, save, and interface.

evidence.claim: PlayStation describes Returnal around repeated death, a changing world, and restarting the journey while breaking the cycle.
evidence.notes: Supports explicit separation between repeated run state and continuity across cycles.
